utterances.text: If it were hit by seven projectiles, it would be damaged; correct? Not just broken windows, it would be damaged if it were hit by -- you would accept that, would you, that if the church were hit by seven projectiles, it would be damaged?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The projectiles that we had, contact shells or ammunitions or mines, and when they -- they would be fired from a tank. And when they impacted on the stone from which the church was built, they would actually explode outwards, so the stone itself would not sustain damage because it was quite solid. Only the gun-powder gases would leave a trace and a black shadow on the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Sir, I put to you that the truth is the church was not being used for any military purpose and the church was targeted to send a message to the Croats living in Kijevo. Isn't that true? Yes or no, sir.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not true. That is not true. The church was used for military purposes. The cemetery was used for military purposes; even individual graves, tombs. And actually we pulled out the captured MUP members from the graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Let's talk about Vrlika. Vrlika, as you say, was taken after Kijevo; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vrlika was taken on the 28th of August -- actually, deblocked, the siege was lifted on that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And in Vrlika looting occurred by everyone, except for JNA troops. That is, it occurred by the TO and the police; and the police allowed trucks with goods that had been looted to leave Vrlika to go to Knin, right?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I only know what my units under my command did, and I can assure you that there was no looting on the part of JNA members.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Let's talk about Drnis. You say it was attacked on the 16th of September, 1991. Now, the military facilities that you talked about in Zitnic and Trbounje - I've probably mispronounced them, but I think you know what I'm talking about - those are not located in Drnis, they are located outside of Drnis; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, both facilities are outside Drnis. One in the territory of Promina, as I've explained, and the other installation is at the end of the Drnis-Sibenik road.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Both of these villages are visible on the map at page 30 of the atlas.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, these facilities have been blocked for only four days when the attack occurred on the 16th of September, 1991; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had been blocked before also, but the general attack was launched on the 16th of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: By the 17th of September, the centre of Drnis was destroyed. Isn't that true, sir?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, that is not correct. We met with the greatest resistance in the part of Drnis towards Sibenik where there was a tower, and the part of town precisely populated by Serbs. There were about a thousand Serbs of the 8.000 population of Drnis who were there, and there the forces of the 113th Brigade of the ZNG and MUP members were deployed, and that is where we met with the greatest resistance. That area was put under fire control as it --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But, sir, I'm a little confused because the action, I thought, was to lift the blockade of these military facilities which were outside -- some number of kilometres outside of Drnis. There was no military reason to attack Drnis, was there, sir?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, the military facility of Zitnic is after Drnis, not before Drnis. But -- and the task which I was given was not only lifting the blockade from the Zitnic military installation but of the entire Sibenik garrison, which at that time was coming under intensive attacks by the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well -- but -- okay. But the Sibenik garrison is a long ways away from Drnis, right?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true, that it is a long ways from it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Okay. And after the centre of Drnis was destroyed, there was wide-scale looting by the police, the TO, and by the JNA. Isn't that true, sir?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, on the 17th of September, when I passed with my unit through Drnis, the command of the 9th Corps by an order established a town command as a military formation in Drnis, and the town commander is my equal in terms of duty, equal to me as the commander of the brigade. And my task was to go in the direction of Sibenik and to lift the blockade of the garrison. It is true that there was looting, and it is also true that I wrote notes to the commander of the corps, seeking that measures be taken against the perpetrators of that activity. There are records of my -- of my warnings and information to the authorities of Krajina to take measures in order to protect property. For instance, there was a --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Sir, sir --

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- pig farm which I insisted should be protected. And there was a tank, water tank for the supply of water.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Sir, but the looting was done by the police, the TO, and by the army. Isn't that true? Everybody was looting.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say that, confirm that, for you, decidedly. But what I can tell you is that such practices of looting were there by various members. I had a check-in point -- I had a point outside Drnis, and there I seized all looted property, which I then sent on to the Knin logistics base.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Let's --

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And some resources, vehicles and such, would be sent to the police station in Knin. This was actually -- as for the further procedure that was in keeping with the law, if the owners reported, things would be returned to their owners; and if not, that would be handled by the commissions, and I don't know what exactly the commissions did. In fact, I know some details which I can describe for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: There's no need. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If we could look, please, at an ECMM report which is ERN 00185371, and I believe, but I'm not certain, that there is a B/C/S version of this report. Yes. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: This is a report -- it's dated the 19th of November, 1991. It's a report from the ECMM on statements about violations of the Second Protocol to the Geneva Conventions concerning Drnis and the villages in the municipality of Drnis.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And if we could turn, please, to 5385 in the English, which is page 15 of the report. And on the B/C/S, I don't, unfortunately, have the exact reference but I'm sure we can find it. It's -- I'm seeing puzzled looks all around.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah, I don't seem to be getting 5385.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Isn't it 5371 and then dash and then -- page 15?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Yes, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I was -- I'm sorry. I was reading the ERN number, the last four digits of the ERN number at the bottom, but maybe -- oh, I see, it was loaded in with a different number. So I see that's why. I apologise. Now, the B/C/S is going to be more of a challenge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Is it with the heading "confidential"?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Yes. But there are several pages that have that heading -- they all have that heading, in fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: 3.2, attack on Drnis, and this is page 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Black is closing in on it, I can tell. There it is. There it is. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now if we could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Sometimes we are even faster than Mr. Black.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We beat him to it this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: -- for unusual learning, maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If we could -- I'm interested in 4.2.1 at the bottom there. And it's talking about what happened in Drnis and it says: "The night between the 16th and 17th, the city was shelled with artillery" -- it says "CNG," but I think that's supposed to be -- that's a reference to "ZNG was situated 4 kilometres south of the city, and the only military object in the town, the police station, wasn't hit at all. Only civilian dwellings were hit. The water and electricity supply to Drnis was cut, except for three Serbian villages." And then the next paragraph, 4.2.2, talks about damage that occurred in Drnis according to one witness. The music school was burned to the ground, civilian homes burned, centre of Drnis.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you see all of that, sir, and can you confirm that that's --

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And that's what happened, isn't it, sir?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it doesn't say here when this music school was burnt to the ground. Was it on the -- between the 16th and the 17th or at the end of October? It doesn't say here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, it says --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: On the 18th of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, to be fair it says: "The following is based on the testimony of Mr. Matic who visited the town 12 days after the attack."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Where do you --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That's in 4.2.2.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But my question to you is: Those things occurred as a result of the attack on Drnis; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you an answer to that, to the effect whether it's correct or not. It is stated here that there had been certain irregularities but without an indication of the perpetrators or the date. What I can tell you is that on the 17th -- from the 17th the forces under my command were not in Drnis because there was a town command established, and you can see that from JNA documents --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But, sir --

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- Mr. Perovic, I believe -- Colonel Perovic was the town commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But, sir, already by the 17th of September, 1991, the centre of Drnis was virtually destroyed; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, the centre of Drnis was not at all completely destroyed. In the centre of Drnis there was several vehicles which were used as barricades which were put there by units of the 113th Brigade. There were tank trucks and some engineers' resources which were a barricade intended to block us from passing through Drnis. In fact, later I organised -- they provided my machinery for those -- that equipment to be removed and all those resources were stationed near the bus station in Drnis. And that is why it all appeared to be demolished there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So it just appeared to be demolished, but it wasn't, in fact, demolished?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I understand. It appeared to be demolished because trucks had been removed from barricading? I thought you said that in the centre of Drnis there were several vehicles which were used as barricades. Just the removal of these vehicles which were used as barricades gave the appearance of Drnis having been demolished? Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether you understood me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's why I'm asking the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- properly. But all these resources, pieces of equipment that had been used to erect the barricade, had been driven into the centre of Drnis near the bus station. And when this is heaped into a heap, it is actually a mess. It looks a shambles. And I suppose someone observing from the side could have concluded that it had all been demolished; whereas, we immediately established communication -- rather, clear the road because my tanks could not go via the mountain but had to pass through Drnis. And that is why that was done. There was no deliberate demolition. We only targeted legitimate military objectives.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's enough. Now, can we get clarity here, Mr. Whiting. When you say the centre of Drnis was demolished, was virtually demolished, what are you referring to? Are you referring to buildings or are you referring to vehicles and things that were used to blockade the road?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I was referring to buildings, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Isn't it true that buildings in the centre of Drnis were destroyed by the attack on the 16th and 17th of September, 1991? Isn't that true, sir? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, we targeted selected targets in Drnis, and the buildings which sustained the most damage were those on the exit from Drnis towards Sibenik where there are houses and buildings belonging to Serbs mostly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, it's true, isn't it, that the city was shelled with artillery and mortars during the night between the 16th and 17th of September. That's true, isn't it, sir?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Okay. That -- you've answered the question --

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Outside the town, towards the village of Knezovi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: It's true, isn't it, that water and electricity was cut to the city. That's true, isn't it, sir?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true. No water, no electricity. The water-tower had been hit; I'm not sure by who. And the town's water-supply was cut. It was I who organised for my own water tanks to bring water to the citizens there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, there were three Serbian villages, Tepljuh, Biocic, and Miocic, which are in the area of Drnis that had water. Isn't that true? Their water-supply was not cut; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, as far as I know those villages were not part of the same water-supply system. They were not connected to the same water-supply system. In those villages the residents drew their water from so-called water tanks dug into the ground, and it was from there that they got water for their houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And you say that the water tank in Drnis was hit. Well, I take it it was hit by Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't confirm who exactly was hit or what, but it certainly wasn't the water-tower in Drnis. The one in Drnisko Polje was hit, a huge water-tower in Drnisko Polje, and that's what resulted in the cutting of the water-supply.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If we could turn to the next page of the document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just get clarity. The one in Drnisko Polje, who was it hit by?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't say with certainty --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That's enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could turn to the next page of the document and look at paragraph 5.3. It says -- it says: "Drnis, according to the crisis committee, all the churches in Drnis were deliberately hit and this should be proved by the fact that all the houses around them were also destroyed."

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That's true, isn't it, sir?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not true. Let me tell you this --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That's fine. That's fine, sir --

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- the first time I saw --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If you say it's true, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could this document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit Number 984.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: By the way, sir, it's true, isn't it, that some Croats who were captured in Drnis were detained and taken to the old Knin hospital prison in Knin; correct? Or do you not know about that?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know about four of them being captured, one of them seriously wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Were -- were any --

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were wearing uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Were any of them taken, to your knowledge, to the old hospital detention centre or unit or facility in Knin?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Whiting, the witness may not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I understand --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: The background is the --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I should put it better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: -- sounds misleading.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Were you aware that the old hospital in Knin was used to detain prisoners of war who had been captured in fighting -- or not in fighting but prisoners of war that had been captured? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I'm aware of is the following facts. All POWs were sent to MP units in the military remand prison in the southern barracks or the Ljubicic or what have you. I don't know. The hospital, if you allow --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Yes, if you could just focus on my question. Do you know that the old hospital in Knin was used to house prisoners of war in September of 1991? Are you aware of that, or no?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time the old hospital was a place where the additional battalion of the 9th Corps was stationed. Later on, however, when the JNA moved out, the old hospital was made over into a prison under the leadership of the justice ministry of the Republic of the Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And when do you say that occurred? What's the date that that occurred, that it became a prison?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was after the JNA had moved out. The Republic of the Serbian Krajina --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What's the date?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- organised for such places -- well, I can't -- I think -- I assume, rather, that it could have been sometime about the second half of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Okay. So to your knowledge before the second half of 1992 the old hospital was not used as a prison?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I knew of.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the additional battalion of the 9th Corps was stationed there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Can you give us a date when this unit was then moved out of this place -- when this battalion left the old hospital?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For as long as the JNA were there, this facility was being used to hold the additional battalion of the 9th Corps. Once the JNA had moved out -- because this was something that we borrowed from somebody; it was not a military facility. Then this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ....

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- fell under the justice ministry of the Republic of Serbian Krajina. Rather, they took it, their government, but I can't give you an exact date because this is not exactly the sort of issue that I dealt with, I mean the ministries and the government. I was into army-related matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you ever, yourself, go to the old hospital in Knin during 1991 for any reason?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, never, not at the military remand prison in -- or, rather, I never set foot in the old hospital or in the military remand prison in the southern barracks --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Sir, that's fine --

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- There were friends who were being held there whom I knew to be honourable people, and yet they were arrested.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I would like to pursue, if you will allow me, just if I can, the question by Judge Hoepfel. You say, sir, that you were not into government issues, you were in the army. I think the question is about the army. The question is: When, to your knowledge, did the JNA leave the hospital? You should be able to know that. That is an army issue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The JNA withdrew from that area on the 19th of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Which year?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1992, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You see, now you know about it. Thank you, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I think it's a convenient time. I'm about to start a new topic, so I think it's a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Whiting. I just wanted to write this date. That brings us to the end of the day for today. The matter stands postponed to Monday, the 23rd, at 9.00 in the morning in Courtroom II. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 23rd day of October, 2006, at 9.00 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
